title: feat(import): face picks follow their SolidCraft names at a re-import
body:
Stacked on #4364 (#4212). This PR is opened against `main`, so it holds the commits of #4364 under its own. Until #4364 merges, review only the 9 commits that "Commits of this PR" lists. Part of #3915.

**Test state, in short:** the first 6 commits were built and tested on the earlier base `773736856` (results below). The rebase onto `a721fd4dc` was not built here. The last 3 commits were never compiled: one is a code fix with a new test, two are docs and comments. Please test it with your runners.

## What changes

A model from a SolidCraft `.sc` file can import again after a change in SolidCraft. Then a face or patch pick inside an operation can lose its geometry id, and today the operation refuses until the user picks again. Now such a pick follows the face that has the same SolidCraft names. The follow is in the undo step of the update.

- **The match** (`camcraft_geometry::source_follow`, D8). A pick follows only when the names leave no doubt:
  - its id was in the old revision only, and no other old feature of the same kind has the same names;
  - each old name and each new name is verified;
  - exactly one new feature of the same kind has the same names, and it is new. A record face's former name counts too (the pieces of a Split Face);
  - that new feature answers to no other old feature's names;
  - a face keeps its plane kind.
- **The stores** (D7): the source selection, the extra and open boundaries, "Do not touch", and the two deburr exclude lists. A Probe pick or a Slot pick never follows, because its pick set the operation's numbers.
- **The review line** (D5): each operation with a followed pick gets one `needs_review` line. The line holds the post until `mark_operation_reviewed`. The line is cleaned and cut to 240 bytes, so the project file always opens (D10).
- **The report** (D6): a pick that cannot follow stays as it was, and generation refuses it as before. The window's re-import message names each such pick with its reason. The `cam.import` / MCP `import_model` answer gets the new key `picks`.
- **The project file** (D4): a model saves its source face record under the new optional entity key `source_faces`. `PROJECT_VERSION` does not change. A record that does not read, or does not tile the facets, is dropped with a logged note. The key never refuses a project.
- **The facet order** (D8, not compiled yet): the follow builds the features of the two revisions from their facets. It does not read them from the features caches. Those caches key a mesh by an order-free digest (`feature::digest_of`), so a hit can carry the facet order of another mesh with the same triangles. The record names facets by index, so the follow would give a face the name of another face.
- **Not followed:** setup WCS and alignment picks, fixture-locate picks, electrodes, chains and vertices.
- Nothing changes in `operation/mod.rs`. There is no new crate dependency and no new test binary: the tests join `model_link` and the geometry lib.

## Maintainer questions (open on #4213)

- **Q1: a version step or not.** The code adds no step (D4). An old reader drops the key and reads the model as today: it loses only the follow (the `solids` #917 precedent). On 2026-11-27 the last release, v0.27.0, writes v82, and `main` writes v84. If this PR merges before the cut that ships v84, each released build that opens the file knows `source_faces`. If it merges later, a released v84 build drops the key. A step is one line in `project/file.rs`.
- **Q2: follow automatically, or as a step that the user accepts.** The code follows automatically, with a review line that holds the post (D5). `posting::review_problems` refuses the post, and `cam.verify` reports the operation as holding the post, until the user marks the operation reviewed. An accept step costs a new command and its MCP tool.

## Commits of this PR

Built and tested on the earlier base `773736856`, then rebased without a build:
- `803a0337e` feat(geometry): find a missing face's successor by its SolidCraft names
- `4b8016b27` feat(project): save a .sc model's source face record, with no version step
- `19154a8b8` feat(import): face picks follow their SolidCraft names at a re-import
- `9647755aa` test(import): land the follow fixtures through ImportModel::source_faces
- `9d34f05ff` fix(import): no follow for Probe and Slot picks, and no two picks on one face
- `54c9a03eb` test(import): the review-line pin generates a facing pass, not a pocket

Never compiled:
- `90ec352b4` fix(import): the name follow builds its own features, not a cached facet order (code and the new test `model_link::facet_order`)
- `aca171657` docs(decisions): D4 holds with v83 and v84 not in a release yet (docs only)
- `22f99b4b7` docs(decisions): file the face-name follow decisions under #4213 (docs, and the provenance comments of three `.rs` files)

## Tests

The pinning tests (33):
- `camcraft-geometry` lib, `source_follow::tests` (14): the match rules, on a box at two widths and a faceted cylinder.
- `camcraft-app` lib, `commands::update_model_follow::{report,stores}::tests` (7): the review line, the report, the walk over each pick store, and the Probe and Slot exclusion.
- `camcraft-app --test model_link` (12): `follow` (7), `face_record` (4) and `facet_order` (1, never compiled), beside the suite's 9 earlier tests.

Results on the earlier base `773736856`, at the head that holds the first 6 commits (2026-11-26):

| Step | Result |
|---|---|
| `cargo test -p camcraft-geometry --lib source_follow` | OK, 14 of 14 |
| `cargo test -p camcraft-app --lib update_model_follow` | OK, 7 of 7 |
| `cargo test -p camcraft-app --test model_link` | OK, 20 of 20 (11 of this PR, 9 earlier) |
| all 40 `camcraft-geometry` targets; `camcraft-kernel` lib, `solidcraft_import`, `solidcraft_hostile` | OK |
| `camcraft-app` lib (325 tests) and the 371 app suites that quick's rules map to this diff, in 4 runs | OK, 0 failed |
| `camcraft-ui` lib (1713 passed, 8 ignored) and the 15 mapped UI suites | OK |
| `cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings` on geometry, cl, gcode, tools, post, sim, motion, app, gpu, ui and kernel | OK |

- The first run found one red pin, a test-setup error: a 2D Pocket reads a picked top face as its floor. `54c9a03eb` makes the pin use a Face op. The follow itself was right.
- **The full batch did not run.** This diff changes `crates/geometry/`, so `cargo xtask gate quick` turns into the batch tier. The batch builds each debug test binary first, and that needs about 169 GB, which the PC did not have. The steps above ran in its place: the suites that quick's rules map to the diff, all geometry suites, and batch's clippy step.

**Please run on your runners:**
- all of the above on the final head;
- `model_link::facet_order` two times: with the change in `UpdateModel`'s follow (`commands/update_model_follow.rs`, `plan`: the two `feature::features_of_facets` calls) and without it (put back `model::features_of_shared`). Without the change it must fail at the `src_of` assert and show the back face. Any other failure means the test does not reach the hazard.

**Not exercised:**
- the full batch and the light lane;
- a real pair of `.sc` revisions (the tests use mesh blocks with records of our own, landed through `ImportModel::source_faces`);
- the window's file watcher, and the fixture re-import route (`ImportFixture`);
- the follow time on a large model, and the wasm build.

**Owed (small):** one sentence for the `picks` key in `docs/agents/mcp-tools.md` (made with the reference command). The "migration" wording on the review banner's hover text (`ui/src/egui_app/op_page.rs`) and in the MCP `mark_operation_reviewed` description.

Changelog: A face or patch pick on a model from a SolidCraft `.sc` file follows its face by the SolidCraft name when the model imports again. The operation gets a review line that holds the post until it is marked reviewed, and each pick that cannot follow is named in the re-import message and in the `picks` key of `import_model`. The project file saves the model's source face record under the new optional key `source_faces`.
Effort: high

Fixes #4213
